findings.title: [P2] Redact provider errors before recording calibration failures
findings.body: `_calibration_needed_exit` stores `str(_exc)` as `message_redacted` and interpolates it directly into stderr JSON. Anthropic constructs this exception from the remote error message, so a provider or proxy response that echoes credentials or sensitive prompt content exposes that content in operator logs. Apply the existing redaction helper before both recording and printing the message. The supplied `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` covers this case.

findings.cross_file_justification: anthropic_adapter.py (diff-touched) classifies any HTTP 400/413 whose body matches is_context_limit_message() as ProviderContextLimitError and fills input_tokens/limit from parse_context_limit(_msg), i.e. from the provider's free-text error body. cheval.py's _calibration_needed_exit then persists those numbers via _ceiling_record_observed into the observed store that _observed_for() reads on every later invocation.
findings.description: Numbers parsed out of a provider error body (or, when absent, cheval's own estimate) are written to the persistent observed-ceiling store and become the input bound for all future calls to that (provider, model) until an operator runs the calibration tool. The data is untrusted: a compromised/misbehaving upstream, an intercepting proxy, or any 400 whose message happens to match the context-limit heuristics can set the bound to an arbitrarily small value (e.g. 'prompt is too long: 1 tokens > 1 maximum'), after which every request preempts at the gate with exit 7 and never reaches the chain. There is no plausibility check (e.g. limit >= some floor, limit <= context_window, observed >= estimate) before the record lowers the bound.
findings.failure_mode: Persistent denial of service of the model-dispatch pipeline for the affected model: all subsequent invocations are rejected pre-flight on the basis of a single poisoned error response, with no automatic recovery.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate parsed values before recording: require limit and input_tokens to be within [FLOOR_MAX_TOKENS, context_window], require the observed value to be >= cheval's own estimate (a provider cannot have seen fewer tokens than we sent), and only lower the bound when the parsed numbers are internally consistent (input_tokens > limit). Fall back to recording without lowering (as the 429 path already does) when the message cannot be parsed. Consider an expiry on observed records.

findings.cross_file_justification: The adapter embeds the raw provider error body (_msg) into the ProviderContextLimitError message; cheval.py writes str(_exc) into models_failed['message_redacted'] and into the stderr _error_json line without passing it through a redaction helper.
findings.description: The field is named message_redacted but is populated with the raw str(_exc), which carries the verbatim provider error body. Provider error bodies can echo request fragments or credential-shaped strings; the test test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message asserts redaction here, but the diff as shown does not call any redaction helper on this path (the suite patches redact_payload_strings to identity, so the envelope-level redaction would not satisfy that test either). Same for the stderr JSON which is operator log material.
findings.failure_mode: Secret-shaped content from a provider error response lands in the MODELINV audit envelope and in operator-visible stderr logs, which are typically retained and shipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Run str(_exc) through the existing redaction helper (the same one used for other models_failed rows) before storing it in message_redacted and before formatting the _error_json message; keep only the classification and parsed numbers in the stderr line.

findings.description: The allowlist regex ends in `$` and is applied with re.match(). In Python `$` also matches immediately before a trailing newline, so a catalog value such as 'context-1m-2025-08-07\n' passes the allowlist and is joined into the anthropic-beta header value. urllib/httpx reject header values containing newlines, so this becomes a hard failure of every request on that entry rather than CRLF injection, but the allowlist is weaker than documented and the stated goal ('a request can never add one') relies on it.
findings.failure_mode: A header value with a trailing newline bypasses the allowlist; the request layer then raises on an invalid header, turning a config typo into an opaque transport error instead of the intended ConfigError.
findings.suggested_fix: Use _BETA_HEADER_RE.fullmatch(item) or terminate the pattern with \Z instead of $; additionally reject any value containing whitespace or control characters.

findings.cross_file_justification: calculate_total_cost (diff-touched) multiplies integer costs by the parsed multiplier and casts to int; ledger.create_ledger_entry calls it after the billed request has completed.
findings.description: _mult() accepts any positive float, including float('inf') (YAML `.inf`) or absurdly large values. In calculate_total_cost, int(inp_cost * inf) raises OverflowError, and a huge finite multiplier inflates cost_micro_usd without bound. Because the ledger entry is created after the provider call, an exception here means the completed call's cost is never recorded and the daily spend counter is not updated.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed long_context block causes post-call ledger failures (billed calls missing from the ledger and daily-spend budget) or wildly inflated recorded cost that trips budget enforcement spuriously.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject non-finite multipliers (math.isfinite) and clamp to a sane range (e.g. 1.0 <= m <= 10.0), treating anything else as 'no premium tier' with a logged warning, consistent with how a malformed threshold is handled.
